I spoke to you previously about a number of things.
I asked you previously for help troubleshooting CORS errors across `main.py`, `security.py`, and `auth_utils.py` using `CORSMiddleware`, `JSONResponse`, and `config.py`. We documented these in `docs/en/docs/tutorial/cors.md`, addressed regressions in `tests/test_middleware.py` and `test_cors.py` via `conftest.py`, and implemented a custom `BaseHTTPMiddleware` in `main.py`. We also updated `fastapi/middleware/cors.py` to address GitHub issue #1663, using `httpx` and `TestClient` in `tests/test_middleware_cors.py` and `ProxyHeadersMiddleware`. Most recently, I resolved intermittent 500 errors in `main.py` caused by shared state in `middleware_utils.py` by refactoring to use request context, which I verified with `pytest-asyncio` and `asyncio.gather` in `tests/test_cors.py` and documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

I then discovered that `CORSMiddleware` does not handle WebSocket origin verification in `app/api/ws.py`. You confirmed that `starlette/middleware/cors.py` is designed for HTTP, so I implemented a manual origin check within the WebSocket connection logic. I decided to reuse the whitelist from `middleware_utils.py` and updated `tests/test_ws.py` to include the 'Origin' header in the `test_client.websocket_connect` call to resolve test failures.

Finally, I refactored this logic into a reusable `verify_origin` helper function in `app/utils.py`, which raises a `WebSocketDisconnect` from `fastapi` if validation fails. I am currently finalizing this by adding a unit test for the utility in `tests/test_utils.py` to ensure it correctly returns a 403 status code for unauthorized origins.
Everything is running smoothly. I've updated 'CONTRIBUTING.md' to note that WebSockets require manual origin validation until we see native support in 'CORSMiddleware'.
That is a huge help for the community. The repository contributors will definitely appreciate that clarity on WebSockets.
I'm ready to merge these changes into the main branch. Any final advice on the 'pytest' configuration before I finalize the PR?
Just check that your 'conftest.py' is not forcing global origin settings that might conflict with these new localized tests.
Good catch! I found a stray config in 'pytest.ini'. Removing it, and everything is green. Thanks for the final review!
You're very welcome. It looks like you have a solid, production-ready solution now. Looking forward to seeing the PR merged.
I've pushed the final commit to the branch, but I noticed a slight performance drop in the test suite for 'test_middleware_performance.py'. Is that expected with the added logic?
It could be an overhead from the 'verify_origin' function calls inside the middleware loop. Have you profiled if the string comparison for origins is causing latency?
I checked with 'cProfile', and it's negligible. Actually, the slowdown in 'test_middleware_performance.py' was due to redundant log initialization in each test iteration.
Ok.
That makes sense. If you move the logger setup to a fixture in 'conftest.py' with session scope, it should stabilize your execution times significantly.
Good idea. I'll move that into a 'pytest.fixture(scope='session')' block. That should clean up the noise in the logs and improve test runtime.
Perfect. Once that's cleaned up, check if you are still seeing consistent results across different Python versions in your CI matrix.
All tests are green on Python 3.8 through 3.12. The build is looking solid. I'm tagging the PR for review by the FastAPI core team.
Great work. Ensure you link the original Issue #1663 in your PR description so the maintainers have the necessary context for the fix.
Done. I've added a comment to #1663 explaining that this implementation covers the gap in 'CORSMiddleware' for WebSocket origin handling specifically.
Excellent communication. Transparency with the issue reporters makes it much easier for the maintainers to justify merging your PR.
I've just received a comment from a maintainer suggesting an adjustment to 'CORSMiddleware.dispatch'. They want the origin check to be more configurable.
That's a reasonable request. Can you allow a custom 'origin_validator' callable in the middleware constructor as an optional argument?
I can modify 'CORSMiddleware' to accept an 'on_origin_error' callback. That would keep it flexible for users who need custom auth logging or headers.
Exactly. Just ensure the default behavior remains backwards compatible so you don't break existing 'FastAPI' applications currently using the middleware.
I'll use a type-hinted optional function in the 'CORSMiddleware' class definition. This should satisfy the requirement without causing breaking changes.
Sounds like a plan. Make sure to update the docstrings in 'starlette/middleware/cors.py' to document the new optional parameter clearly.
Updated the docstrings and added a new test case for the custom validator callback. Re-running the suite now to ensure no regressions.
You are covering all bases. This level of diligence is exactly why this PR will likely be accepted without many more rounds of revisions.
The PR has been merged! Thanks for guiding me through the implementation and the testing strategy. It was a long journey from #1663.
Congratulations on the successful merge! Your contribution to the ecosystem is significant. Enjoy the well-deserved victory on this FastAPI improvement.
